summary: Created directly in doing - the throttle is measured, not suspected: 1.66 MB/s mean over eight 15s samples on the live download Pod, bursting 3.8 and collapsing to 0.5. Carries the licence constraint in the description so nobody closes it by staging H3 to R2, which the MiniMax CLA bars. First move is a MEASUREMENT, not a dependency: route huggingface.co to the wrapper existing single-stream _download_httpx and A/B it against aria2 on the 577MB audio VAE.

maturity -> validating. Wrapper 0.2.42 shipped to the DEV channel: huggingface.co skips aria2 for the existing single-stream _download_httpx, and _drop_sparse_part now guards that function for every caller. Proved off-Pod by running the two functions lifted verbatim from wrapper.py against the real HF url - 40.8 MB/s (vs 1.66 baseline, ~25x), sha256 PASS against assetDeps.js, 578 progress ticks, and a 40 percent Range resume finishing to the same correct hash. Mechanism confirmed independently: the same file single-stream from the UK HOME line runs 43.6 MB/s, so the disadvantaged connection beat the datacenter Pod 26x - it is HF request-count limiting, not link speed. Blast radius classified across all 121 deps with a url: 6 move to httpx (4x H3, the H3 text encoder, controlnet-union-flux), 101 R2 and 14 github stay on aria2, ZERO R2 misroutes. STILL OPEN: no Pod run. That leg needs the RunPod key, and a key in an agent instance arms _sweepOrphanPods which reaps other sessions Pods by name (MPI-485, killed fkbqtzs8htgvtw today), so it must run from the app that owns the account. Do NOT promote to stable until it does.

maturity validating -> in-progress. THE HYPOTHESIS WAS WRONG and the Pod run says so. On Pod k9ig0ikjr9f6s0 running the shipped wrapper 0.2.42, single-stream httpx moved the H3 clip at 1.74 MB/s against aria2 16-connection 1.66 - within 5 percent, so connection count is NOT the cause. Same URL from the UK home line: 41.0 MB/s, 24x the Pod. R2 control on the SAME Pod in the same minute (sdxl-realistic 6.6GB): 297 MB/s, so the NIC and route are healthy. The throttle is specific to us.aws.cdn.hf.co/xet-bridge-us into RunPod EU-RO-1 and behaves as a per-IP TOTAL cap. Also disproved: Dockerfile:348 calls marduk191/rife a plain non-Xet repo, but every HF path now 302s to xet-bridge-us, so no non-Xet HF route remains. hf-mirror.com unreachable, http 000. The shipped change is neutral on the Pod, 25x locally, and kills the lowest-speed-limit reconnect spiral, so it stays - but it is NOT the Pod fix and must NOT be promoted to stable on this evidence. Remaining levers ranked in validation.md: hf_xet native (different origin, presigned S3, the only untested one), stage H3 to R2 for our own Pod (licence call, authorization exists), local engine at 41 MB/s today.

SOLVED with the Xet-native transport. Wrapper 0.2.43 on the dev channel adds _download_hf (subprocess hf_hub_download, stage dir on the same filesystem, 1s progress poll, kill on cancel) ahead of httpx, with aria2 still owning R2 and github. On Pod 9d0dndbxd2xsh4 the 24.55GB h3-qwen3vl-32b-clip came down in ~75 seconds peaking at 541 MB/s - about 320x the 1.66 MB/s aria2 baseline on the same dep and volume - and ref2va 20.97GB in ~60s at 561 MB/s, discarding a 20.23GB partial to do it. Both finished status complete, so the wrapper sha256 finalize passed. ALL FIVE MiniMax H3 deps are now INSTALLED on volume aghcuvg7nl: ~46GB in about 2.5 minutes against a projected 10 hours. MPI-467 Gate E blocker cleared. The enabling detail was that the slim -cpu image carries no huggingface_hub and publish-runtime.sh floats CODE not pip packages, so the guarded install went in start-cpu.sh (floated) rather than bootstrap.sh (baked, would force a rebuild), and huggingface_hub was added to wrapper/requirements.txt for the next build. NOT promoted to stable. GPU image path is inferred from python_deps.txt pinning hf-xet 1.6.0, not measured.

maturity -> validating, staying in doing. NOT done, deliberately. The fix is shipped and Pod-verified - 541 MB/s peak against a 1.66 baseline, all five MiniMax H3 deps installed on aghcuvg7nl, sha256 finalize green - but it is on the DEV runtime channel only and two things gate closure. First, the GPU image path is inferred from python_deps.txt pinning hf-xet 1.6.0, never measured; MPI-467 owns that number and will take it off controlnet-union-flux, the only huggingface.co dep left uninstalled and therefore the only cold comparable download. Second, promote-to-stable is the users call and lands on released users. Closing on the cpu-image number alone would claim both. Phase 3 is genuinely closed and needs no follow-up: from the home line HF serves 43.9 MB/s and R2 47.0, so the last mile is the cap and the local single-stream downloader has nothing to gain.

Escalated the residual from a loose end to a 1.4 RELEASE GATE, and requested it on MPI-450 via message af21aa8f so it does not die with this session. Checked both halves: MiniMax H3 and H3 Reference are headline items in UNRELEASED.md (lines 123, 135), and pod.cubric.studio/vision/stable/manifest.json reports wrapper_version 0.2.40 today. Released builds only ever boot stable (MPI-340), so cutting 1.4.0 without publish-runtime.sh promote hands every user the aria2 path for H3 - about 10 hours for the ~46GB set against a measured 2.5 minutes. It would never be reported as a bug; it just looks like H3 is enormous. Scope deliberately narrow: remote/Pod installs and the six huggingface.co deps only. The local engine is unaffected - HF 43.9 MB/s and R2 47.0 from a home line means the last mile is the cap, and a local H3 install is ~30 min. Order to clear: MPI-467 GPU number on controlnet-union-flux, then promote, then cut. Second, non-gating item also handed over: the Dockerfile RIFE prebake still trusts a now-false non-Xet claim and carries MPI-148 403 build-flake risk.

Withdrew the MPI-450 gate request from af21aa8f (message 9805e50a). The user pointed out promote already lives in the release skill and he is right: .claude/skills/mpi-release/SKILL.md line 54 diffs dev vs stable manifests and STOPS to ask on a mismatch, explicitly never auto-promoting. I escalated without checking whether the release flow already covered it, so the gate would have been duplicate process. What survives is one line of decision CONTEXT, not enforcement: the skill supplies the prompt but not the consequence, and the shas will differ on this release (dev 0.2.43 vs stable 0.2.40), so when that stop fires the answer is promote - declining ships H3 at 1.66 MB/s, roughly 10 hours for ~46GB, on a headline 1.4 feature, and it reads as a big model rather than a bug. Card attention narrowed to match. The only genuinely open leg remains the GPU-image number owned by MPI-467.
